Bio: Alessio is a multi-award-winning artist based in Los Angeles, working at the intersection of experimental electronic pop and contemporary classical music. Bösendorfer partnered on his debut album, presented by Yamaha Music Europe. His subsequent releases keep bringing him back to Funkhaus Berlin.

Piano at 5, violin at 9, composition at 11, digital audio production at 15. By 24, five academic degrees — a Bachelor’s and four at Master’s level, all with distinction — from classical piano and composition to film scoring and sound design. Last one at UCLA in 2026, while teaching in its Music Industry program. Trained across Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and California, he speaks five languages and studied Latin and Ancient Greek.

From New York to Hong Kong, he has participated in a diverse range of events, including solo, chamber and orchestral concerts, discographic recordings, radio and television projects, artistic curations, movie productions, conferences, and film festivals. He has won several first prizes in national and international music competitions and received more than a dozen other awards and scholarships.

His value lies not in the range of his training, but in where it meets. His work for Disklavier calls for editing with a producer’s precision while hearing every note with a pianist’s ear. He writes string textures with an arranger’s training and a violinist’s hand alike. When he approaches a Bach fugue, he reads it with a contrapuntist’s mind and the finesse of a mixing engineer balancing its voices. As a result, from first sketch to final master, he can handle every stage himself, or work with engineers and producers in their own language. These are not separate skills he moves between, but a single ear shaping everything he touches.

He studied with Inna Faliks, William Kinderman, Roberto Prosseda, and Marco Biscarini, and worked alongside David Leaf at UCLA. He has taken masterclasses with Boris Berman, Enrica Ciccarelli, Jed Distler, Jean-Jacques Eigeldinger, Francesco Libetta, Andrea Lucchesini, Bruno Monsaingeon, William Grant Naboré, Marcello Nardis, Boris Petrushansky, Matti Raekallio, John Rink, Alexander Romanovsky, Konstantin Scherbakov, and Lisa Yui.
